Description

As explained in #41265, we now have a BCP 47 language tag glossary entry, but many of our pages still link directly to (variants of) the RFC or not at all.

This PR:

  • Links all instances of "BCP 47 language tag" (or similar) to the glossary entry using consistent link text.
  • Removes a couple of old language tag reference links from article text.
  • Adds a better language tag reference to the glossary entry.

Motivation

Additional details

Fixes #41265

In "Example 1: height and width", in the for loop iterating over arrImages an undeclared variable "i" was being used, breaking the example.

Description

A declaration for the variable "i" has been added just before it is used, as well as appropriate incrementation after each use in the loop.

Motivation

A broken example creates confusion.

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: Declared missing variable i in Example 1.

items.content_html:
Description

This PR adds a new page to our list of "attacks", this one is on JavaScript Prototype Pollution.

It's a draft for now. Still trying to learn more about this myself. I want to add another example scenario "Pollution via JSON.parse and object merging/cloning" but I don't fully understand it yet and haven't been able to get myself polluted this way :) Maybe this has been fixed in JS engines? Any pointers appreciated.

Generally, I'm not sure if I covered everything that needs to appear here. I think I'm somewhat happy about the defenses part, but explaining how to actually get into to polluting objects might need some more words?

Also, I think this needs integration into JS docs (at a minimum some linkage).

Motivation

Developing a series of guides about common attacks on websites, explaining for each attack: how it works, the impact, and how to defend against it.

Additional details

Would love some feedback from @wbamberg, @aaronshim and maybe @Josh-Cena.

Related issues and pull requests

None, I think.
items.title: Add a page for JavaScript prototype pollution attack

items.content_html:
Description

Chrome 136 introduces the CSS dynamic-range-limit property; see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146250411769856.

The dynamic-range-limit-mix() function is also supported, but I'm not sure which version of Chrome this first appeared in. I've asked Chrome engineering for an answer to this question.

This PR documents both of the two features mentioned above.

Note

Some of the description in the property page might want to go into a separate glossary entry, but I wasn't sure how best to chop up this information. Opinions welcome.

Motivation

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: Editorial review: Document CSS dynamic-range-limit

items.content_html:
Description

Added single quotes to the strict-dynamic code example

Motivation

I did not read properly (stupid me) and just copied the code example for strict dynamic, only to find out that single quotes are needed for this to work. This is correct in all the textual explanation, but the quotes were missing in the code example.
items.title: chore: add single quotes to strict-dynamic code example

items.content_html:
FF144 (and Safari) implement CSSStyleProperties. This is a derived class of CSSStyleDeclaration that represents the inline or computed styles on an element. It exists because CSSStyleDeclaration is now going to be a base class from which specific types of style and rule information will be applied, and only include the relevant information for that context.

Anyway, this adds the class. Note however that I have not yet updated the things that use it. I didn't think anything did, but in retrospect, Safari likely does.
items.title: FF144 CSSStyleProperties docs

items.content_html:
FF144 adds support for the JS Upsert Proposal in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1979917

This adds a release note that covers the new methods added to Map and WeakMap.,

Related docs work can be tracked in #41134
items.title: FF144 Relnote: JS Upsert Proposal

items.content_html: Part of #41134
items.title: Reference for stage 3 upsert

items.content_html:
Description

There are still several Learn articles not linked from the learnsidebar. The ones we want to keep should really be linked in some way. This PR adds an "Additional tutorials" subsection at the end of the extension modules to contain the additional tutorials.

In one case (performance), I didn't add it into "Additional tutorials"; I just moved the article so that the slug made more sense, and then added it into the main flow of that module.

In one case (forms), I edited an article to make it a) more useful and b) actually make sense in the context of earlier forms articles in the same module (we don't want to cover all those CSS techniques only to then say "don't style form elements" in a later article).

Motivation

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: Add extensions additional tutorials links to learnsidebar

items.content_html:
FF144 aligns with Chrome and Safari such that a cross origin iframe now requires sticky activation in order to redirect the top level page via window.top.location (in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1419501).

This PR adds a release note and also a section in the iframe docs explaining the expected behavior as it is now.

Related docs work can be tracked in #41138
items.title: FF144 Relnote+Doc: Cross origin iframe requires user interaction for top navigation
